transformation_method: Sum of hourly precipitation over window
biological_interpretation: Total volume of antecedent precipitation; candidate environmental factor associated with conidial splash dispersal of Colletotrichum and root-zone soil saturation in literature.
limitations_and_assumptions: ERA5-Land reanalysis smooths localized convective cloudbursts; assumes open-canopy rainfall reaches ground uniformly.

transformation_method: Count of discrete days where 24-hr daily sum > 0.1mm
biological_interpretation: Frequency and persistence of rainfall; candidate factor associated with sustained microclimate moisture and prevention of foliar desiccation.
limitations_and_assumptions: 0.1mm standard meteorological rain-day threshold; does not differentiate between a light mist and heavy downpour.

transformation_method: Count of hourly timestamps where RH >= 80.0%
biological_interpretation: Evidence-supported candidate feature; RH >= 80% is reported in literature as a favorable threshold for fungal spore germination and acervuli maturation.
literature_threshold_vs_derived: Literature-Supported Candidate Threshold Feature (TNAU / Reddy / Palakshappa)
limitations_and_assumptions: 2m open-air humidity; relative humidity within dense turmeric foliage canopy is typically 5-10% higher during daylight.

transformation_method: Count of hourly timestamps where 22.0°C <= temperature_2m <= 32.0°C
biological_interpretation: Thermal incubation window reported in literature for favorable mycelial growth and lesion expansion for Colletotrichum (21-32°C) and Taphrina (25-30°C).
limitations_and_assumptions: Open-air ambient temperature at 2m; does not account for canopy shaded thermal buffer or radiant leaf heating.

transformation_method: Arithmetic mean of hourly 2m temperature over window
biological_interpretation: General metabolic thermal context; warm dry regimes (>28°C) reported to favor aphids while moderate regimes (24-28°C) favor foliar fungi.
limitations_and_assumptions: Linear average masks diurnal thermal extremes that may cross upper/lower pathogen tolerance thresholds.

transformation_method: Count of hourly timestamps where (temperature_2m - dew_point_2m) <= 1.5°C
biological_interpretation: Atmospheric proxy for foliar surface dew condensation; free water film is biophysically associated with fungal appressorial penetration.
limitations_and_assumptions: Derived meteorological proxy from open-air dew point; does not directly measure physical leaf surface wetness duration.

transformation_method: Volumetric arithmetic mean of topsoil moisture (0-7cm)
biological_interpretation: Elevated topsoil moisture (>0.30 m³/m³) associated with sub-canopy boundary layer humidity and rhizosphere saturation.
limitations_and_assumptions: Model-derived land surface hydrology (HTESSEL scheme); does not account for local field soil texture (red loam vs clay) or raised ridge drainage.

transformation_method: Arithmetic mean of hourly 10m surface wind speed
biological_interpretation: Stagnant air (<5 km/h) associated with moisture retention; moderate breezes (8-18 km/h) reported to assist airborne ascospore transport of Taphrina.
limitations_and_assumptions: 10m surface wind does not reflect aerodynamic drag and boundary layer calm within dense turmeric foliar rows.

transformation_method: Arithmetic mean of downward surface shortwave solar flux
biological_interpretation: High solar flux accelerates foliar evaporation and UV exposure; overcast skies associated with moisture retention.
limitations_and_assumptions: Macro-grid downward radiation; does not capture intercropping shade (e.g. coconut / marigold) or self-shading.

transformation_method: Count of hours between 06:00 and 18:00 where shortwave_radiation < 150 W/m²
biological_interpretation: Indicator of persistent cloudiness during daylight; associated with prolonged foliar moisture retention.
limitations_and_assumptions: Astronomical daylight hours proxy; cloud cover thickness not directly differentiated.

transformation_method: Categorical stage mapped from Days After Planting (DAP)
biological_interpretation: Phenological context: Vegetative (60-120 DAP) and Rhizome (120-180 DAP) are documented susceptible stages; Senescence (>180 DAP) hypothesized to have reduced active lesion spread.
limitations_and_assumptions: Supplied via agronomic calendar/farmer input (unavailable in weather data); varietal maturity timing differences (e.g. BSR-1 vs Alleppey Supreme).
